what: CPU work started by the producer session or its reviewer sessions while a Qwen baseline reservation was timing requests (B4 and Q27, positions 16-63 and 64-127). Disclosure only: no interference correction is applied to any recorded time.
method: Windows: the reservations' start and end events in gpu_ledger.jsonl. Jobs: the producer's session transcript and the reviewer sessions' transcripts (tool calls with timestamps; a foreground command ends at its result, a background one at its completion notice), and, for the diagnosis runs, the run directories' output times. File edits, sleeps and waiting loops are omitted. Machine load: logs/cotenancy_qwen_*.log (1-minute load average of all processes, sampled every 30 s); reproduced by `python -m scaling.perf_report --corrections`.
isolation: The Qwen runs were pinned to cores 5-9,15-19 (Cortex-X925) and these jobs to 0-4,10-14 (Cortex-A725). Pinning separates cores only: the GB10's CPU and GPU share one unified LPDDR5x memory, so memory-bandwidth contention is not excluded. Processes of other sessions on the host, if any, appear only in the load average.

jobs.kind: the pilot's CPU diagnosis (diagnose.py; torch, 8 threads, 4-6 SQL workers)
pre-freeze reviewer probe scripts (5 runs of 5-58 s)
phase-1 verifier checks (short runs; one 85 s mutation test)
phase-2 verifier development and runs (3 SQL worker processes, torch 4 threads), including a 7-minute full run 09:46:07-09:53:24
decision-rule and serving previews over the saved records

scope.B4 thinking, positions 16-63: about 31 of 81 minutes had a producer or reviewer job running (mostly the 18-minute diagnosis); the load average exceeded 6 in 44% of samples (max 28.4)
scope.Q27 thinking (low), positions 16-63: about 8 of 119 minutes; load average above 6 in no sample (max 6.7)
scope.B4 thinking, positions 64-127: about 27 of 96 minutes (09:28:01-09:54:37); load average above 6 in 6% of samples (max 8.2)

not_known: Which individual Qwen requests ran during these jobs: the records carry durations, not start times. The size of any slowdown: none was measured, and none is subtracted.
